newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan ministers arrive for talks.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan ministers arrive for talks.

text.p: The foreign ministers of India and Pakistan arrived for talks in New Delhi on Wednesday at a time of rising hopes the longtime foes could defuse half a century of tension.

Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart Gohar Ayub Khan arrived separately at a former prince's palace in the Indian capital for a breakfast meeting expected to last about one hour, authorities said.
Gujral warmly greeted the visiting Pakistani minister, putting his arms around Khan in a hug, and the two men stood hands clasped before photographers ahead of the breakfast talks.

It was the first meeting of the two nations' foreign ministers since the south Asian neighbours resumed high-level talks last month and came during expectations that their prime ministers would meet on the sidelines of a regional summit next month in the Maldives.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since 1947 and the last negotiations had broken down in 1993 over Kashmir, where India is fighting a separatist revolt.
On Tuesday, Khan said he would not allow the fresh negotiations to reach a deadlock and was prepared to "talk and talk and talk" until the two sides settled their differences.
